title: A stale /codon_start overrides SnapGene's readingFrame, so real vendor CDSs are translated in the wrong frame
description:
`applyReadingFrame` (lines 150-169) only uses `readingFrame` when the feature has no `/codon_start` qualifier. When both exist and disagree, it keeps the qualifier and warns "/codon_start was kept". For |readingFrame| = 1 it returns early, so a stale codon_start of 2 or 3 is kept with no warning at all.

Real SnapGene files show the reverse precedence. In files from SnapGene's own plasmid library (snapgene.com fetch.php), the CDS carries a stale `<Q name="codon_start"><V int="1"/></Q>` next to `readingFrame="±2"`:
- T-Vector pMD20: lacZα, +, rf=2
- T-Vector pMD19 (Simple): lacZα, −, rf=−2
- pTZ57R/T: lacZα, −, rf=−2
- pUC57-T: lacZα, −, rf=−2

In all four, SnapGene's own stored `/translation` matches frame |readingFrame| (checked with Biopython translate) and never frame codon_start. PlasmidPop found the same in SnapGene 8.2's bundled files (issues #153 and #164, which also list pDrive, pPrime, pSTBlue-1, pT7Blue and BlueScribe-mEGFP with rf=−3).

Consequences:
1. `translateFeature` on the parsed record gives the wrong protein: pMD20 lacZα reads `IGSPGTELEFTGRRFTTS*LGKPW…` instead of SnapGene's `SDPRVPSSNSLAVVLQRRDW…`. In the real-file run, 4 of 12 CDSs fail and the other 8 match.
2. `writeGenbank` exports `/codon_start=1` next to a frame-2 `/translation`. Biopython, translating the exported record with its own `/codon_start`, disagrees with the `/translation`.
3. A `parseSnapGene` → `writeSnapGene` round trip drops `readingFrame="2"` (the written Feature element has no readingFrame attribute), so SnapGene itself would then show the CDS in frame 1.

The implementer's test 'records readingFrame 2/3 as /codon_start' (`src/io/snapgene-read.test.ts:338`, the 'frame conflict' case: readingFrame=2 with codon_start=3, expecting 3) and oracle case `tools/oracle/snapgene_oracle.py:911` encode the wrong precedence, so the suite stays green.

Fix direction: when a readingFrame attribute is present, set `/codon_start` to |readingFrame| and replace any existing codon_start qualifier. That also covers frame 1 when a codon_start qualifier exists. Keep the qualifier only when the attribute is absent, as with third-party writers.
expected: `/codon_start` = "2" (|readingFrame|, replacing the stale "1"), and `translateFeature(rec, cds, { toStop: true })` === `"SDPRVPSSNSLAVVLQRRDWENPGVTQLNRLAAHPPFASWRNSEEARTDRPSQQLRSLNGEWP"`, i.e. SnapGene's own stored translation. GenBank export should carry `/codon_start=2`, and a SnapGene round trip should keep `readingFrame="2"`.
actual: `/codon_start` = ["1"], with the warning 'Feature "lacZα": readingFrame="2" disagrees with /codon_start=1; /codon_start was kept.' `translateFeature` returns "IGSPGTELEFTGRRFTTS" (the full frame-1 text is `IGSPGTELEFTGRRFTTS*LGKPWRYPT*SPC…`). `writeGenbank` emits `/codon_start=1` beside the frame-2 `/translation`, and Biopython confirms the mismatch. `writeSnapGene` emits `<Feature recentID="0" name="lacZα" directionality="1" type="CDS" allowSegmentOverlaps="0" consecutiveTranslationNumbering="1">` with no readingFrame. On the four real library files, 4 of 12 CDSs fail to reproduce SnapGene's stored translation.

title: A valid file with more than ~125k features (65,536 on WebKit) returns no record
description:
readSnapGene collects features with `features.push(...parseFeatures(root, seqLength, dna.topology, warnings))` (snapgene.ts:186). Primers use the same pattern at :189. The spread passes one argument per feature. Past the engine's argument limit it throws RangeError. Measured in Node 22/V8: 100,000 features work and 140,000 fail. MDN documents a hard-coded 65,536-argument limit in JavaScriptCore, which is the Tauri webview on macOS and Linux and the planned iOS viewer. The defensive catch in parseSnapGene (snapgene.ts:237-240) turns the error into `records: []` with a single 'unexpected error' warning and drops any warnings collected before it.

The file itself is valid:
- writeSnapGeneWithWarnings writes it with zero warnings, so a large GenBank record saved as .dna cannot be reopened.
- Biopython 1.88 reads the same 32 MB file correctly: 10,000 bp, 140,000 features, first [0:5](+) 'f0', last [139:144](+) 'f139999'.

This breaks the spec contract: exactly one record, or none plus a warning only when the data is not a SnapGene DNA file. Fix: append in a loop (`for (const f of list) features.push(f)`), or use concat. Do the same for primers.
expected: One record with 140,000 features and no warnings, as Biopython reads it.
actual: records: [] and warnings: [{ message: 'Could not read the SnapGene file: unexpected error (Maximum call stack size exceeded).' }].

title: Invalid UTF-8 in XML packets becomes U+FFFD with no warning
description:
readXmlPacket (snapgene.ts:130) decodes every XML packet with decodeUtf8 (snapgene-binary.ts:255). That function replaces each ill-formed byte with U+FFFD and reports nothing. A features or notes packet written in ISO-8859-1 or Windows-1252, as a third-party writer or a damaged file can produce, is imported with silently corrupted units and symbols: 'µg/ml' becomes '�g/ml', '®' and '°' become '�', and warnings is []. By contrast:
- The DNA packet reports every non-IUPAC byte it replaces (snapgene-sequence.ts:127-131).
- Biopython rejects the same file with "UnicodeDecodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0xb5".

The spec says corrupt data → warning, and the task rules prefer explicit warnings over guessing. Fix: count replacements in decodeUtf8, or compare against the input, and add one warning per packet.
expected: At least one warning naming the packet, e.g. 'packet 0x0a at offset N: K byte(s) are not valid UTF-8 and were replaced by U+FFFD'.
actual: The note reads 'G418 50 �g/ml (Geneticin�)' and the description 'grow at 37 �C', with warnings: [] (the 'expected 0 to be greater than 0' assertion fails).

title: Warning messages have no length limit (400 KB message from a 150 KB packet)
description: readXmlPacket (snapgene.ts:133) copies fast-xml-parser's error text into the warning unchanged. For unclosed tags that text is a pretty-printed JSON dump of the whole open-tag stack. A 150 KB features packet of '<a>' therefore produces a single 400,154-character warning, 2.7 times the input. Other warnings also copy untrusted text in full: a 50,000-character feature name or segment range gives a ~50 KB message ('Feature "nnnn…": unknown directionality …'). A React warning list or toast then has to render hundreds of KB to MB of text, and a damaged or crafted file can scale this further. Fix: truncate embedded values and the parser error (e.g. to 200 characters plus '…').
expected: A short warning (under ~2,000 characters) saying the features packet is malformed.
actual: A 400,154-character warning: 'Could not read the features of the SnapGene file (packet 0x0a at offset 35: Invalid '[    "Features",    "a",    "a", …' repeated 50,000 times.

title: Reader hangs for minutes on a crafted XML packet: whitespace run before '=' makes XMLValidator.validate quadratic
description: parseXml (snapgene-markup.ts line 95) calls fast-xml-parser 5.11.2's XMLValidator.validate on every untrusted XML packet before parsing it. When the validator's attribute tokenizer (scanAttributeTokens in node_modules/fast-xml-parser/src/validator.js) meets a '=' with no attribute name before it, it restarts at tokenStart + 1. Each restart rescans the whole whitespace run in front of the '=', so a run of k spaces, tabs or newlines inside any tag of any XML packet (features, primers, notes, sequence properties) costs O(k^2). On the same string XMLParser.parse takes 1-2 ms and validate takes 7.1 s at 80 KB. Measured parseSnapGene times: 10 KB 130 ms, 20 KB 414 ms, 40 KB 1.7 s, 80 KB 6.9 s, 100 KB 9.4 s, 250 KB 58-66 s. Extrapolated, a 1 MB file takes about 18 minutes. This breaks the spec ('Truncated or corrupt data -> warning, never an exception or an infinite loop') and the module's own documented guarantee ('its own processing is linear in the file size'). Opening one downloaded .dna file freezes the app or its worker. A possible fix: skip XMLValidator on untrusted text (XMLParser plus a try/catch already reports malformed packets), or reject tags whose attribute text has a nameless '=' before validating.
expected: The file is read in linear time, well under 2 s for 100 KB, returning one record plus a warning (or the feature).
actual: 9,440 ms for a 100 KB file. 250 KB files block for 58-66 s; time grows with the square of the whitespace run.

title: The module's own test suite is red: 2 failing tests (CI 'npm test' fails); the report says all tests pass
description: The current snapgene suite has 173 tests and 2 of them fail on every run, so CI's 'npm test' step (.github/workflows/ci.yml) fails. The implementer's report says 'All 144 tests in 7 files pass'. (1) snapgene-oracle.test.ts > 'notes_two_packets.dna': compareRecordWithBiopython (testkit.ts:241) requires the record's division to match Biopython's on SYN. Biopython takes the division from the last Notes packet only (UNC). The reader merges Notes packets on purpose, as documented in snapgene-notes.ts, and returns SYN, which the oracle's own 'expected' record agrees with. (2) snapgene-robustness.test.ts:292 'clips untrusted text quoted in warnings' expects 11 warnings. The current code returns 12 (per scenario: 1+2+1+1+1+1+2+2+1). Both are stale expectations: the source and testkit were edited at 12:53-12:56 and the tests were not re-run. The project rules require tests to be green.
reproduction:
cd /home/srdgjuchdr/HHereditas/packages/core && npx vitest run src/io/snapgene
# -> Test Files 2 failed | 5 passed (7); Tests 2 failed | 171 passed (173)
# FAIL snapgene-oracle.test.ts > SnapGene handmade edge cases vs oracle > notes_two_packets.dna
#   AssertionError: notes_two_packets.dna: expected [ 'division SYN vs UNC' ] to deeply equal []
# FAIL snapgene-robustness.test.ts > SnapGene reader: warning size > clips untrusted text quoted in warnings
#   AssertionError: expected [ …(12) ] to have a length of 11 but got 12
expected: All snapgene tests pass, as the report states.
actual: 2 of 173 tests fail on every run, so CI would be red.

title: writeSnapGeneWithWarnings silently drops reverseColor and GenBank header metadata, though its contract says every loss is reported
description: SnapGeneWriteResult.warnings is documented as 'Everything that could not be represented exactly in the SnapGene format', and the report says the function 'reports everything the format cannot store'. The module header (snapgene.ts lines 46-47) also says reverse colours are 'dropped (with warnings)'. In fact no writer code handles Feature.reverseColor: it is dropped with no warning. Saving a GenBank-imported record as SnapGene, the common conversion path, also silently drops meta.version, meta.source, meta.keywords and every meta.extraHeaderLines entry: REFERENCE blocks (authors, titles, PubMed IDs) and DBLINK. That is 24 header lines for pUC19_M77789.gb and 133 for pBR322_J01749.gb, with 0 warnings, even though SnapGene Notes can store References. A UI that uses these warnings to tell the user what 'Save as SnapGene' loses shows nothing. The GenBank -> SnapGene integration test claims 'nothing is lost silently' but never compares meta.
expected: One warning for each kind of dropped data (reverse colour, version, keywords, source, references and other header lines), as the API contract and module docs promise.
actual: Both warning arrays are empty. The read-back record has no reverseColor, version, source, keywords or extraHeaderLines.

title: Writer warnings print 0-based half-open coordinates in 'a..b' notation and give the wrong reason for reversed segments
description: Warnings are shown to users, and DEVELOPMENT.md section 5 says 'User-visible positions are always 1-based' (seq/range.ts formatRange exists for this). describeRange (line ~347) prints `${start}..${end}` with a 0-based start and an exclusive end, in the same notation GenBank uses for 1-based inclusive ranges. Example: a segment {start:-10,end:10} on a 100 bp circular record is reported as 'written as 90..110'. The file actually stores SnapGene range '91-10' (bases 91-100 plus 1-10), and '90..110' does not exist on a 100 bp plasmid. In writableSegments (lines ~370-372), any linear segment with start > end gets the reason 'is outside the N bp sequence', so a reversed segment inside the sequence ({50,40} on 100 bp) is reported as out of bounds. Both mislead the user about where the problem is.
expected: 1-based display such as 'written as 91..10', and a reason like 'start is after end' for the reversed linear segment.
actual: 'Feature "f": segment -10..10 is not in normalized form; written as 90..110.' and 'Feature "g": segment 50..40 is outside the 100 bp sequence; not written.'

title: Writer emits Notes elements that its own reader rejects, so a round trip loses the whole Notes packet with no writer warning
description: For records with meta.sourceFormat 'snapgene', unknownNotesElements writes each unknown meta.extras key as a Notes element if it matches XML_NAME (/^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_-]*$/). XML_NAME accepts 'constructor', 'prototype' and '__proto__', which fast-xml-parser 5.11.2 rejects with '[SECURITY] Invalid name'. parseSnapGene then skips the whole Notes packet, so description, organism, accession, comments, Created/LastModified and UUID are all lost on read-back. The writer gives no warning. Keys 'toString', 'valueOf' and 'hasOwnProperty' are silently renamed to '__toString' and so on when read back. The reader tests already accept that such names wipe the packet on read, so the writer should skip these keys with a warning rather than produce a file it cannot read back.
expected: The description, organism and accession survive the round trip, or the writer skips the key and warns.
actual: The writer reports no warnings. The read-back description is '', organism and accession are undefined, and the read warning is 'Could not read the notes of the SnapGene file (packet 0x06 at offset 575: [SECURITY] Invalid name: "constructor" is a reserved JavaScript keyword that could cause prototype pollution); they were not imported.'

title: SnapGene's '?' (ambiguous codon) is kept in /translation instead of the INSDC code 'X'
description: `cleanQualifierValue` removes two SnapGene notations from /translation so that the value follows INSDC rules: the commas between segments and the final '*'. SnapGene also writes '?' for a codon that contains ambiguous IUPAC bases, and the reader leaves that '?' in place. '?' is not an INSDC amino-acid code; the feature table requires 'X' for an unknown residue. Two problems follow. (1) A GenBank export of a record read from SnapGene writes /translation="...?...", which is invalid INSDC. (2) The stored /translation no longer matches HHereditas' own `translateFeature`, which gives 'X' for the same codon. This occurs in SnapGene's own plasmid library. I checked 1,706 stored translations from 428 library files downloaded from snapgene.com (kept only in the scratchpad, not committed). After the reader's clean-up, only two differed from our translation for a reason other than the alternative-start convention of the translate module: pAd/BLOCK-iT-DEST AmpR residue 183 (codon NCA) and pJW168 Rep101(Ts) residue 289 (codon YAT). In both, SnapGene stored '?'. Every other check on 493 real SnapGene files passed: 6,578 feature locations matched Biopython; readingFrame equals ±codon_start; sticky-end signs were checked against T-vectors (-1/-1) and directional TOPO vectors (downstream +4, bottom-strand 5' CACC overhang); writer round trips changed only documented things.
expected: /translation = "MX". SnapGene's ambiguous-codon marker '?' should be mapped to INSDC 'X', in the same way the reader already removes SnapGene's segment commas and final '*'. That way the value matches translateFeature and gives a valid GenBank /translation.
actual: /translation = "M?". The '?' is kept, so a GenBank export contains an invalid character, and the value disagrees with translateFeature's 'MX*'.
